notes.gomesi: In Ankole women wear the omushanana, a draped cloth, rather than the Buganda gomesi.
notes.eno: Egi for n- nouns: eshaati egi, this shirt.
notes.nimevaa: Njwaire, I’m wearing (I have put on).

guidebook.intro: Name your clothes, say what you’re wearing and shop for something that fits. “My” and “this” agree with each piece of clothing.

tips.title: My with different nouns
body: Nouns starting with **e-** plus **n** or **m** (class n-) take **yangye** in the singular and **zangye** in the plural: **eshaati yangye**, **empare yangye**. Clothes words in **ebi-** take **byangye**: **ebiraato byangye** (my shoes).

tips.title: This agrees too
body: “This” changes with the noun: **eki** (ekintu), **egi** (n- nouns), **ogu** (people and omu- nouns), **aba** (people, plural). **Eshaati egi** is “this shirt”.
To wear is **-jwara** and to take off **-juura**: **Ninjwara eshaati** (I’m putting on a shirt), **Njwaire** (I’m wearing).

culture.title: Omushanana
body: Women in Ankole wear the **omushanana** for weddings and ceremonies: a long, flowing cloth draped over one shoulder. Men wear the **ekanzu**, a long white robe, often with a jacket.
